name: Tour du Mont Blanc
description: The classic Alpine loop around Mont Blanc through France, Italy and Switzerland, counter-clockwise from Les Houches. The track links the stops; passes without verified coordinates are placed along it.

les-houches.name: Les Houches
les-houches.text: The classic start, at the foot of Mont Blanc.

col-de-voza.name: Col de Voza
col-de-voza.text: The first pass, with the tramway rattling past.

les-contamines.name: Les Contamines
les-contamines.text: A chalet village in the Montjoie valley.

col-du-bonhomme.name: Col du Bonhomme
col-du-bonhomme.text: A windswept pass on the old Roman road.

les-chapieux.name: Les Chapieux
les-chapieux.text: A hamlet famous for its Beaufort cheese.

col-de-la-seigne.name: Col de la Seigne
col-de-la-seigne.text: The border with Italy, and the first sight of the Italian side of Mont Blanc.

courmayeur.name: Courmayeur
courmayeur.text: The Italian halfway town, below the south face.

grand-col-ferret.name: Grand Col Ferret
grand-col-ferret.text: The highest pass of the tour and the border with Switzerland.

la-fouly.name: La Fouly
la-fouly.text: A Swiss village under the glaciers of Mont Dolent.

champex.name: Champex-Lac
champex.text: A village around a mountain lake.

trient.name: Trient
trient.text: A pink church below the Trient glacier.

col-de-balme.name: Col de Balme
col-de-balme.text: Back in France, with the whole Chamonix valley ahead.

lac-blanc.name: Lac Blanc
lac-blanc.text: The famous lake mirroring the Mont Blanc massif.

chamonix.name: Chamonix
chamonix.text: The town of the first Winter Olympics, 1924.

les-houches-return.name: Back in Les Houches
les-houches-return.text: Three countries and ten thousand metres of climbing later.

story.three-countries: France, Italy, Switzerland: the tour crosses all three around one mountain.
story.glaciers: Glaciers hang above the path, smaller every decade.
story.home-stretch: The needles of Chamonix rise across the valley: almost home.

facts.tmb-length: The Tour du Mont Blanc is about 170 km with around 10,000 m of climbing; most people take 10 to 11 days.
facts.mont-blanc: Mont Blanc, 4,806 m, is the highest mountain in the Alps and in Western Europe.
facts.race: The Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc runners cover the whole loop in about 20 hours.
facts.1924: Chamonix hosted the first Winter Olympic Games in 1924.
